chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the slaughter (dhabihah), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Face your slaughtered animal toward the Qiblah, and do not cut its spinal marrow (nakha') until it dies, and do not eat from a slaughtered animal that was not slaughtered from its proper place of slaughter.'

key_terms.الذَّبِيحَة: dhabihah — the Islamic ritual slaughter or the slaughtered animal; a key concept in halal food law
key_terms.النَّخْع: nakha' — the act of cutting the spinal cord or severing the nape of the neck; prohibited in Islamic slaughter until after death
key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: qiblah — the direction of the Ka'bah in Mecca, toward which Muslims pray and toward which animals should face during ritual slaughter
key_terms.الْمَذْبَح: madhbah — the proper place of slaughter on an animal's throat/neck; slaughter must be performed from this specific location

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic rulings on proper ritual slaughter according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) provides three essential rulings for valid Islamic slaughter: the animal must face the Qiblah, the act of nakha' (severing the spinal cord) is prohibited before death, and eating from an animal not slaughtered from the proper throat area is forbidden. These rules reflect the Islamic emphasis on minimizing animal suffering and ensuring ritual correctness. The question was posed by Muhammad ibn Muslim, one of the closest companions of the Imam, who transmitted thousands of jurisprudential rulings.
word_analysis: cut its spinal marrow (before it dies)

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the slaughter, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Face the Qiblah by your slaughter, and do not flip it over until it dies, nor eat from a slaughter what you did not slaughter from its proper place of slaughter’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about slaughtering. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must turn the animal to be slaughtered toward al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah) and do not cut its spinal cord before it dies. You must not use for food what is not properly slaughtered from the proper place.’”
